$comment: Tone -> visual style. Edited by hand; no code change needed to retune it.
A tone is a description of DELIVERY measured locally from the audio (loudness
and pitch relative to the speaker's own median, speaking rate, pauses). It is
NOT emotion recognition. Keep the styling restrained: if a viewer can tell
which rule fired, the rule is too loud.
tones.<name> fields, all optional:
fontFamily  a family name from `caption-engine fonts`. Omit to inherit.
bold        true forces the real bold face. Omit to inherit.
scale       0.5-2. Tone scale and --active-scale MULTIPLY, so keep this
near 1.0 (0.9-1.15) or lines will reflow.
color       #RRGGBB. Omit to inherit the base caption colour.
active: active-word appearance. An explicit CLI flag beats these.
thresholds: classifier tuning, merged over the built-in defaults. Units are
semitones relative to the SPEAKER'S OWN median pitch, and energy in units of
the clip's own spread - never absolute Hz or dB, which mean nothing across
different recordings.
minConfidence gates everything. With --tone-scope cue (the default) it is
compared against the share of a caption line that agreed on a tone, so a line
whose words disagree keeps the base style. Tones apply only with --prosody
(or --tone-style auto).
FONTS: tone-driven font switching works, but only fonts present in
assets/fonts are selectable. The shipped theme therefore varies weight, scale
and colour only. Add Inter/Poppins/Anton/etc. and set fontFamily per tone.
motion: kinetic-captions defaults (version 2+). Entirely optional and only
ever consulted when --motion is not none.
template       default --animation-template (a name from
`caption-engine --help`, under --animation-template).
intensity      default --motion-intensity, 0..1.
toneTemplates  per-tone template choice for --animation-template auto.
An explicit --animation-template/--motion-intensity on the command line
always wins over these.
